title.zh: 要求高等教育机构报告所有大学体育项目的参与情况与项目支持支出的法案
title.en: An Act Requiring Higher Education Instituttions to Report Participation and Program Support Expenditures in All College Athletic Programs
title.orig: An Act Requiring Higher Education Instituttions to Report Participation and Program Support Expenditures in All College Athletic Programs

source.name: LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation）

completenessNote: 全文，共 11 条；逐字取自 LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation） 官方页面（statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11180_2019.html），未改写、未摘译、未节选；原文语言：英语。 条文抬头依源文为 “Section N.” 等形式，本库统一规范为 “Section N.”；首行抬头与条内标题的分段依源文块级边界还原。

text.en: Short Title. - This Act shall be known as the Athletic Programs Report Act".

Declaration of Policy. - It is the policy of the State to promote physical education and encourage athletic programs, league competitions and amateur sports, including training for international competitions, to foster self-discipline, teamwork, and excellence towards the development of a healthy and alert citizenry. All educational institutions are also mandated to undertake regular sports activities throughout the country in cooperation with athletic clubs and other sectors. In line with these objectives, both male and female athletes shall be given equal opportunities to received proper training and participate in sports activities and competitions.

Publication Duty of the CHED. - The CHED shall be compile and publish annually in its webaite or in a newspaper of general circulation, the reports containing the information collected from the HEIs, including the athletic conferences recognized by intercollegiate athletic associations and participated in by the HEIs.
Reportorial Requirement. - The CHED shall submit the reports required under Section 4 of this Act to Congress on an annual basis.

Sanctions. - Pursuant to Section 8 of Republic Act No. 7722, otherwise known as the "Higher Education Act of 1994", the CHED shall impose disciplinary sanctions against an official or an employee of a HEI found violation Section 5 of this Act.

Implementing Rules and Regulations. - Within sixty (60) days upon the effectivity of this Act, the CHED, in coordination with the Philippine Association of State Universities and Colleges, Coordinating Council of Private Educational Associations, the Association of Local Colleges and Universities, and the POC issue the necessary rules and regulations to fully implement the provisions of this Act.
Separability Clause. - If any provision or part hereof is held invalid or unconsitutional, the same shall not affect the validity and effectivity of the other provisions.

Repealing Clause. - All laws, executive orders, decrees, instructions, rules and regulations contrary to or inconsistent with any provision of this Act are hereby amended, repealed or modified accordingly.
Effectivity. - This act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation.
